summary.name: Smorza
summary.one_liner: A free, open source menu bar volume mixer for macOS that gives each app its own volume, mute, and output device.
keywords: control volume of each app mac
route app audio to different output
use_cases: Lower a browser or call app so music stays louder
Mute a single noisy app without pausing it
Send a video call to headphones while games stay on speakers
Adjust volume keys to affect only the app in front
Keep per-app levels saved across restarts and device changes
summary.what_it_does: Smorza runs in the menu bar and lets each app that plays sound have its own volume, mute, and output device. It can route different apps to speakers, headphones, displays, or AirPlay, and falls back to the default output when a device is unplugged, then restores the app's setting when it reconnects. It uses audio taps built into macOS 14.4 rather than a virtual sound card, and browser helper processes are grouped into one row per browser. Settings such as volume, mute, and output are saved per app bundle ID and per output device. An optional Pro tier adds profiles, auto-ducking, boost to 200%, and global mic mute.
notable: No audio driver or system extension; built on macOS 14.4 audio taps
Open source under the MIT License, installable via Homebrew tap
Per-app volume, mute, and output device saved per device and restored on reconnect
Browsers and Electron apps grouped into one row via helper processes
caveats: Cannot control individual browser tabs; volume and output apply to the whole browser
Not notarized by Apple, so macOS requires a manual approval on first launch
Requires macOS 14.4 Sonoma or later; macOS asks for audio capture permission
Pro tier ($2.99 once) is described as coming soon; core features are free
